rules_text:
Rules summary You are captaining a starship through a newly-discovered galaxy. Your mission: to recruit a crew of alien species and robots, synergizing their skills to earn points. During the course of the game, you will deploy 5 ships. Each will land on, then explore, new worlds. Collect sets, fulfill objectives, set off combos. Contents 1 COMPONENTS: 2 HOW TO PLAY 3 GAME END 4 POINTS COMPONENTS: Captain cards (black border): ~ Everyone starts with only a captain card in play. ~ The captain's occupation (skill) symbol in the upper right corner counts toward set completion. ~ The card also features a bonus action track that is triggered whenever a Veteran card is put into play. Each captain has a unique set of bonus actions. Crew Cards: (specialists, emissaries and robots) Specialists (blue border, animal head symbols) ~ Comprised of 6 different animals that can be collected for points. ~ Each has an occupation symbol (top right of card) that can be collected for points AND used in combos. Emissaries (brown border, clipboard symbol) ~ These grant points at the end of the game for meeting objectives. ~ These also animals that count toward set collection Robots (green border) ~ These are worth points (as shown inside a yellow hexagon in the top right corner). ~ May have an occupation symbol in the top right corner. Veterans (medal symbol) ~ Specialists, Emissaries and Robots can all be veterans. Look for a medal symbol at the top left corner of the card to indicate whether they are a veteran. ~ Putting a veteran into play earns an immediate bonus action Planets: Each planet card has 2 landing spaces on the bottom and 2 exploration spaces at the top. Each grants an action: draw cards or play cards. You must land a ship on a planet before you can explore it. ~ Some planets feature a condition that must be met before the action can be taken, such as discarding a card from your hand or having specific symbols in play. You may not land a spaceship there unless the condition has been met. ~ Two planet cards are undiscovered. They are not available to land on and explore until you have put 6 crew and 9 crew into play respectively. ~ If you're not able to land or explore, you must pass your turn. Spaceships: Plan wisely - you only have 5 ships to place. After landing, a ship can explore one time. HOW TO PLAY On each turn, you will land or explore, then resolve the planet's action. COMBOS occur when you play a card. Most crew have an ability on the bottom left of the card. These are triggered immediately when played. ~ Some abilities may require you to meet a condition (such as having a robot or specific occupation in play). If the condition is not met, you can still play the card, but you can't use the card ability. GAME END Game ends after 10 rounds, once everyone has landed AND explored with their 5 spaceships. POINTS Points are only earned for cards that you put into play during the course of the game. Cards in hand have no value. SETS OF THE SAME ANIMAL: ~ the 1st 2 animals aren't worth any points ~ 5 points for the 3rd animal ~ 5 points apiece for each additional animal in the sets SETS OF DIFFERENT ANIMALS: ~ 15 points for each set of all six different animal species EMISSARY CARD OBJECTIVES: ~ Earn points as described on the card ROBOTS ~ Earn points equal to the amount in the hexagon symbols on all of your robot card VETERAN BONUS ~ Each captain card gives points for the 4th veteran you put into play. If you don't put 4 into play, you don't receive these points.

---

A new Galaxy has just been discovered on the borders of the Empire! Commanding your Spaceship, you go explore this new Eldorado, full of treasures and mysteries. Planet after Planet, your discoveries allow you to build up your Crew. Hire Specialists and Robots to benefit from their abilities. Attract Empire Emissaries on board, which will entrust you with new missions, worth Credits. Grab your part of the wonders that this new Galaxy is full of, to become the wealthiest explorer !

Wild Space is a tactical card game in which you aim at combining your cards efficiently. Each time that you add new cards to your collection, you reinforce your Crew, earning Credits and preparing  your next combos. Wild Space carries all the excitement of the best combo card games, within short plays and with accessible rules.

How to play ?
Wild Space carries all the excitement of combo card games, with accessible rules. On each turn, a fresh action selection system offers you two simple types of options : add a new card to your Crew or draw new cards. When you play a card, you trigger its ability if the cards in your Crew fulfill its condition. Putting new cards into play is therefore useful for getting powerful abilities right now, but also for gathering the conditions for triggering future abilities. Learning how to plan your actions is key for triggering efficient combos and being able to put several cards into play at once. And knowing that the Credits that you need to get at the end of the game in order to win are based on how your Crew is composed only emphasizes that.

—description from the publisher
community_text:
[Rating: 2/10] Sold on 2021-04  : I would like to love this game : + You can create few combo between cards + There is a "marketplace" for competition between players + The graphics pf the cards are wonderful - No interaction / competition between players  it is a race to victory point, so a multiplayer solo - I would expect more combo, be able to fight other players - Probably a game for very young players

[Rating: 3/10] I don't understand games like this. Players are almost completely detached from each other, you play for yourself, optimising your layout, scoring a point salad at the end. What is fun about it? Beats me.

[Rating: 3/10] Played this at a friends house.  It is essentially a set collection game where you are either doing actions to draw some cards or play a card.  The problem here is that it relies very heavily on being able to chain cards together (one card allows you to play another card with a certain icon to play another card with a different icon etc.). It's a cool idea in theory and leads to some satisfying plays but it almost always just comes down to the luck of the draw and who can get more cards with icons that chain together.

[Rating: 3/10] Game about making combos, which you make, if randomness let you do so. Completely nothing interesting, no single element I can say was fun.

[Rating: 3.6/10] Does nothing to distinguish itself, ok game but unoriginal.  Simple point-salad type game.

[Rating: 4/10] It's not bad, but it really is far from anything to write home about.  The mechanic of being so limited by 10 actions seems attractive at the beginning but the game just ends up being a total point salad without any real interaction with the other players. Essentially, all you do is draw from 4 stacks of cards, filter and discard and play what you have, regardless of what the other players do. So, there a lot better games with similar gameplay out there. The design is nice, though.

[Rating: 4/10] Wild Space has cool artwork and the most beautiful colour palette meeples I've ever seen (they are spaceships, but I would love to see those divine players colours in all games just in different shapes). It's fun but it won't stay in my collection.??

[Rating: 4/10] Generic set-collection/combo-building game lacking either interesting synergies or satisfying combos. Maybe for kids/families. Could potentially be improved by expansions.

[Rating: 4/10] Mechanics are solid, art is great and the it plays easy. That said, the game feels like it lacks agency, since there is only so much you can do to mitigate the card draws and flops. I'd play it again, but won't seek it out.
